minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved starting the new Building Commissioner at a set grade and step, and planned outlier review.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed job description revisions and the proposed pay grid, agreeing to identify "outlier" positions that sit oddly in the grid before applying any rating tool. It approved the hire of a Building Commissioner at a recommended grade and step. The next meeting was set for May 24 so members can bring their outlier lists.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted, by roll call with all in favor, to hire the Building Commissioner at the recommended grade and step.
The committee agreed to identify "outlier" positions that sit oddly in the proposed pay grid before applying any rating tool.
Members will review job descriptions in the shared folder and bring their own outlier lists to the next meeting, set for Wednesday May 24 at 5 p.m.
Discussion noted that some positions' proposed maximums dropped compared with the current grid, which could upset employees who would reach the ceiling sooner.
A staff member said her revised job description was missing from the final document and agreed to resend it for comparison.

why_it_matters: The proposed pay grid sets the pay range for town jobs, and lower maximums for some positions would change what long-serving employees can earn.
The step chosen for a new hire sets a starting wage for a town department head, which becomes part of the town payroll in the budget residents vote on.
watch_next: Personnel Committee meeting on Wednesday May 24 at 5 p.m., where members bring their outlier lists.
The revised job description to be resent for comparison with the final document.
